findings.title: Existing local recovery-code credentials are not removed when credential is written to user storage
findings.body: When updateCredential returns true, the method only logs and does not create or replace the local recovery-code credential. If the user already has a locally stored recovery credential (for example created before the external storage supported recovery codes), that credential remains in Keycloak's database. Because recovery codes are supposed to be replaced when regenerated, stale local credentials can keep old codes valid and undermine credential rotation.

findings.title: Local credential removal is used for credentials that may be federated
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential can now return a federated credential supplied by a user storage provider, but the cleanup path calls removeStoredCredentialById. That method removes credentials from Keycloak's local store, not from an external user storage. If the last recovery code was consumed in a federated credential, this call may silently do nothing or use an id that is not meaningful locally, leaving the external credential state inconsistent with the required-action logic.

findings.title: Missing null checks for hidden form fields can cause NPE
findings.body: The hidden form fields generatedRecoveryAuthnCodes and generatedAt are read with getFirst and then used without null checks. If a POST to the required action omits one of these fields, generatedAtTimeString.equals(...) or generatedCodesString.split(...) throws NullPointerException. This turns a malformed or replayed form submission into a server error instead of re-challenging or failing gracefully.

findings.title: Unsafe Optional.get and next-code get can throw during login
findings.body: The constructor calls credentialModelOpt.get() and then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() without verifying that a credential exists and that an unused code is available. If the recovery credential is missing, was removed concurrently, or all codes are used, the login page bean throws and the user gets an error page instead of a graceful challenge.

findings.title: Plaintext recovery codes are passed to external user storage
findings.body: The helper serializes the generated recovery codes in plaintext and passes them to the user storage via UserCredentialModel. The local path stores only hashed codes, but an external storage that persists the supplied challenge response (as the test storage does) will store recoverable one-time codes unhashed. This weakens the security model for federated storages unless hashing is explicitly documented or enforced.

findings.title: No coverage for fallback to local storage when user storage does not support recovery codes
findings.body: The new test makes BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage support recovery codes, so it only verifies the user-storage branch. There is no test in this change for the fallback path where the user storage does not support recovery codes and Keycloak should create the credential locally. Since the PR's purpose is to support both locations, that fallback should be covered.
